incentives.name: Data center sales and use tax exemption
incentives.law: 2023-25 state budget (2023 Wisconsin Act 19); from a 2023 bill by Sen. Romaine Quinn and Rep. Shannon Zimmerman
incentives.what: Exempts certified data centers from the 5% state and local sales taxes on purchases to build and equip facilities
incentives.value_known: Legislative Fiscal Bureau: about $1.5B forgone during construction plus $369M per year once built (more than $2B total) for Beaver Dam, Mount Pleasant, Port Washington and Epic (Verona)

dockets.what: Very Large Customer (VLC) and Bespoke Resources tariffs for data centers. Approved with changes Apr 24, 2026: 15-year minimum term, threshold lowered from 500 MW to 100 MW, VLCs pay 100% of generation costs, transmission cost protections. We Energies asked to reopen June 10; Oracle sued over credit-rating rules.
Electric Service Agreement to serve the Beaver Dam data center; approved with a stronger termination charge and safeguards May 7, 2026; Alliant ordered to file a standalone large load tariff
NSP asked the PSC for its own very large customer rate structure (credit bar BBB-); docket number not found

laws_and_bills.name: 2025 AB 1036 / SB 969 (ban on data center NDAs; Rep. Clint Moses)
laws_and_bills.what: Would prohibit nondisclosure agreements intended to conceal information about a data center from the public. Introduced Feb 13, 2026; failed to pass Mar 23, 2026 when the session ended.

laws_and_bills.name: 2025 AB 840 / SB 843 (data center requirements; Rep. Zimmerman, Sen. Quinn)
laws_and_bills.what: Would keep costs of infrastructure mainly serving a data center off other ratepayers, require on-site renewables serving the load, closed-loop cooling, annual water-use reports to DNR and reclamation bonds. Passed the Assembly 53-44 on Jan 20, 2026; Senate committee recommended concurrence 3-2; Senate failed to concur Mar 23, 2026 (session ended).

laws_and_bills.name: 2025 AB 472 / SB 502 (nuclear tax credit; very large customer tariffs)
laws_and_bills.what: Nuclear generation tax credit plus PSC approval of electric tariffs for very large customers. Passed the Assembly 86-11 on Jan 22, 2026; Senate failed to concur Mar 23, 2026.

laws_and_bills.name: 2025 AB 1162 (very large customer class; Rep. Spaude)
laws_and_bills.what: Would have the PSC create a very large customer class for electric utilities. Introduced Mar 19, 2026; failed to pass Mar 23, 2026.

laws_and_bills.name: 2025 Wisconsin Act 16 (AB 140; SB 122 companion)
laws_and_bills.what: Creates s. 66.1105(17)(i): for a 'data center district' (a TID whose project costs all relate to a certified qualified data center), the 12% TID value limit findings do not apply; covers Port Washington TID 5 (if created before Jan 1, 2028) and Beaver Dam TID 10. Such districts may not allocate positive increments to other districts. Signed July 8, 2025.

local_rules.what: One-year data center moratorium, adopted unanimously

Two-year interim zoning ordinance with moratorium after voters approved village powers 54-3 Note: Wisconsin Watch (Apr 29, 2026) reports town electors voted 44-0 on Apr 16, 2026 to authorize zoning authority, then the ordinance banned data centers for up to two years; the 54-3 figure in the earlier source may be a different vote (not reconciled).

local_rules.place: Clark, Dane, Dodge, Door, Grant, La Crosse, Rusk, Shawano counties; City of Superior; villages of Ashwaubenon, Wrightstown, Baldwin, Greenville; towns of Beetown, Bloomington, Waterloo, Westport, Hampden, New Denmark, Big Bend
local_rules.what: Listed by Wisconsin Watch among at least 22 local data center moratoriums as of July 6, 2026 (individual ordinances not opened)
Voters approved requiring voter approval for future TIF districts over $10M; business-backed lawsuit pending

Advisory referendum Aug 11, 2026 on supporting data center infrastructure: nearly 9 in 10 voted against; NetChoice threatened legal action. Village moratorium adopted June 2026, extended to one year in July.
Policy requiring town board approval for data center NDAs

Plan Commission voted 5-0 on Oct 5, 2026 to recommend a temporary development moratorium of up to 12 months on rezonings and land divisions enabling data centers, and created a DC-O Data Center Overlay District (data centers conditional only in the overlay)
County board policy barring supervisors from signing data center nondisclosure agreements
